title: Raga Bihagra
hookLine: a raga for late at night, colored by separation

cards: The house is asleep. The dishes are done, the phone is face down, and the only light is a lamp or a streetlight through the curtain.
At this hour some people find themselves talking to their own heart, quietly, the way you'd talk to a child who can't sleep. Daytime is loud enough to drown that voice out; night isn't.
The Granth has a raga for this hour, and in it a Guru speaks to his own soul. This week began at dawn. It ends here, at night.

teach.h: A NIGHT RAGA, COLORED BY SEPARATION.
teach.b: Bihagra is a night raga. Tradition sets it for the late hours, and its mood is colored by separation, the ache of being apart from the one you love.
In the Guru Granth Sahib that ache has a direction: the beloved is God, and the one waiting is the soul.
Guru Ram Das has chants in Bihagra that keep calling to the singer's own soul with a tender word, jindurie, something like my dear life, my little soul, urging it again and again toward the Name.
It's how a person might talk to themselves late at night, when sleep won't come: come on, dear one, remember what matters. This isn't despair. In these chants, separation is a kind of love.

teach.h: LONGING MEANS THE BOND IS REAL.
teach.b: You only miss what you're bound to; the longing is the sign the bond is real, and the hymns turn the ache into a reason to remember.

teach.h: THE WEEK: DAWN, QUIET, GENTLE, NIGHT.
teach.b: Now look back at the week, because the ragas made a day. Asa met the dawn with hope, opening with a hymn that hears all creation singing at God's door.
Gujri, quiet devotion, with a crane flying far while her chicks are cared for. Devgandhari, gentle, a Guru admitting the mind won't listen, and a short hymn heard twice.
And now Bihagra, at night, longing. The same Word, through different hours.

how: Shabads headed Bihagra are sung in that raga in kirtan, and tradition places it in the late hours of the night; its chants by Guru Ram Das and Guru Arjan are sung as songs of the soul's longing for God.

o: a lullaby raga for putting children to sleep
a raga of anger, sung against enemies
a night raga of longing, the soul apart from God

games.q: a week of ragas — tap the pairs.

s: in the Granth, the longing of Bihagra is for a lost human love
the beloved is God, and the one waiting is the soul.
Guru Ram Das's Bihagra chants call to the soul with a tender word
jindurie, something like my dear life, my little soul.
separation in this poetry means despair
you only miss what you're bound to; the longing is a sign the bond is real.

games.q: it's late, and you miss someone badly. in Bihagra, what does the longing become?
o: a reason to remember the Name.
something to push away until morning.
games.why: the Bihagra chants keep calling the soul, my dear life, back toward the Name. the ache becomes the reason to remember.

practice: Dim whatever you can, the screen, the lights, your eyes, and listen to the late sounds that come far apart, a distant car, the house settling, letting the silence between them be part of what you hear.
If a longing rises in one of those gaps, let it come, and let it settle back into the quiet without chasing it. If you pray, set one Waheguru into a gap; if you don't, simply rest in the spaces.

wordCard.voice: Raga Bihagra. A night raga colored by separation, where Guru Ram Das calls to his own soul as my dear life. Today's word.
